Dense lazy seeds

Source: R/lazy-dense.R
lazy-dense.Rd

A StoreDenseSeed is a DelayedArray seed for a dense Element on disk, in h5ad or zarr (v3 and v2). It holds an open store handle and the path of the array and reads blocks with the store layer's selection reads (array_read()), so one code path serves every format. The seed has the shape of the array in Python's order, which is the order of the R array, so no transposing is needed.

Usage

store_dense_seed(
  store,
  path,
  chunks = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env(),
  strings = FALSE
)

# S4 method for class 'StoreDenseSeed'
dim(x)

# S4 method for class 'StoreDenseSeed'
dimnames(x)

# S4 method for class 'StoreDenseSeed'
extract_array(x, index)

store_dense_values(x)

Arguments

store

An open store handle, see io-store.

path

Absolute path of the dense array.

chunks

Optional chunk shape, one entry per dimension.

call

The call reported by errors.

strings

Whether a string array is accepted (type character, used for string columns of lazy data frames).

x

A StoreDenseSeed.

index

A list with one entry per dimension, NULL (every index) or a vector of positions.

Details

Its type() is fixed from the On-disk dtype and not from a read, because a small h5ad selection of int64, uint32 or uint64 comes back as integer where a whole read gives double. The types are those of read_h5ad(): integer for int8, int16, int32, uint8 and uint16, logical for bool and double otherwise. Blocks are plain arrays, so use store_dense_values() to get the values with the On-disk dtype record that read_h5ad() gives. Reading int64 or uint64 values of magnitude 2^53 or more raises the error of read_h5ad() when the block holding them is realised.

chunkdim() is the chunk grid of Python's read_elem_lazy(): the chunks argument if given (NA or -1 for the whole axis), otherwise the on-disk chunk shape (the inner chunk shape of sharded zarr), and for a contiguous HDF5 dataset 1000 or the axis length when that is smaller. The handle must stay open while the seed is used.

Deviations from Python

An int32 array holding -2^31 (the bit pattern of NA_integer_) is read as double by read_h5ad(), but a seed's type is fixed before any read. Realising a block that holds -2^31 therefore raises anndata_dtype_overflow_error, suggesting an eager read. See vignette("deviations") for the full list.
